newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends lower after late sell-off.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends lower after late sell-off.

text.p: CSCE world sugar ended weaker Tuesday and just off its session lows after a late round of liquidation by speculators, market sources said.
With little fresh news to provide impetus, traders were mainly focused on spread activity and position adjustments ahead of March's expiry at the end of the week.
A bout of industry-linked selling dragged prices lower early on, but the market managed to stabilize at midsession, with aggressive short covering in the May contract offering some support.
But the tone reversed again late in the day, as keen selling of the March-May switch took its toll on the overall market.

"As you got through the afternoon, you saw increased pressure on the spread," a trader said. "You're not getting any real follow-through on the upside," he added. "Specs are long in May and not in a position to add any more on."
Most-active May ended down 0.07 cent per lb, at 10.83, having traded from 10.81 to 10.92. Spot March fell 0.12 cent, to 10.80, after touching an intraday low of 10.78.

Traders said the market's direction would hinge in part on May's ability to hold the 10.80 cent level. Additional support was noted at 10.73-10.72, followed by 10.60. Upside targets were pegged at today's ceiling of 10.92 cents, followed by 11.19, a five-month high on the contract set last week.
Traders also expected to see continued pressure on the nearby switch into Friday. May closed at a 0.03 cent premium today, after ending at a 0.02 cent discount on Monday.
An estimated 24,891 lots were exchanged on the day, compared with Monday's official tally of 27,490. ((-- W Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
